_comment: How MANY modifiers and abilities a rolled NPC comes out with. The type x rarity table of NpcTypeDefaults stays the CEILING (how many slots exist); every slot here is a separate chance, and the chances fall off slot by slot. WHICH modifier or ability lands in a filled slot is not decided here - that is the NpcModifiers catalog and the stance archetype.
_formula: slot 0: firstSlotChance * rarityMultiplier; slot i>0: nextSlotChance * decay^(i-1) * rarityMultiplier; clamped to 0..1. Slots are walked in order and the walk stops at the first slot the dice refuse, so the result is a count and never a gap.
_seedWarning: A chance of exactly 1 (or 0) is not rolled - it is decided, and no die is spent on it. So moving any number here ACROSS 1.0 or 0.0, in either direction, changes how many dice a spawn spends and shifts every later draw of that spawn one step along the generator: not only how many modifiers and abilities come out, but WHICH ones. Seeded runs and worlds rebuilt from a seed stop reproducing across such an edit. Nudging a number strictly between 0 and 1 does not.
_requiredFields: Every ladder named below must name all three of firstSlotChance, nextSlotChance and decay. A misspelled field name is refused rather than defaulted, because the only default the arithmetic could take is 1 - which would silently hand that type back the always-maximum spawn. A TYPE left out of a section entirely is the one supported exemption and does mean 'fill every slot'.
_modifiersNote: Calibration point agreed with the owner: Elit x Epic (4 slots) = 90% at least one, 54% exactly one, 24% two, 9% three, 3% all four.
_abilitiesNote: Own numbers, same shape: on a Regular or a Special an ability is an event, on an Elit one or two is the norm. Boss and Archon are absent on purpose - their slot count is 'every ability of the pool' (NpcTypeDefaults.AllAbilities), an authored promise and not a thing to roll against.
_rarityNote: One ladder for both tables: rarity is the same promise wherever it is read. A type or a rarity this file does not name rolls no dice at all - the slot is simply filled, which is the behaviour that predates this catalog.
